topics.topic: Acceptance status of the reopened State 0
questions: Is the reopened State 0 still unaccepted, or do R0-61 to R0-71 constitute acceptance of the revised whole?
Has the current post-R0-71 text been accepted as a whole and closed, or is it still an unaccepted reopened draft?
Has the owner accepted the reopened State 0 as a whole, so later states may treat R0-24 through R0-71 and the revised sections as settled?

quotes: State 0 closes again when its question rounds are clear; the owner then accepts it as a whole.

None open. OQ-01 to OQ-09 were decided by the owner on 2026-10-26 (R0-06 to R0-14); OQ-10 to OQ-12, raised by the vNext reopening, on 2026-10-27 (R0-38 to R0-40); OQ-13 to OQ-18, raised by the emulated question rounds 3 and 4 (`experiments/registry-pochemuchka/state0/`), on 2026-10-27 (R0-47 to R0-52). The answers to question rounds 18 and 19 were proposed to the owner and accepted on 2026-10-27 (R0-61 to R0-71).
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats the revised whole as accepted and lets later states rely on it, while another treats it as an unaccepted reopened draft; the owner and authors of later states notice which decisions are settled.
judgement.why: The text says the questions are clear but does not record the renewed whole-state acceptance that its own close rule requires.

topics.topic: Conditions ensuring retained anonymised-project identifiers and pointers are non-identifying
questions: Under what condition can a retained project id and its uninspected pointers be declared non-identifying, and what happens if either still permits re-identification or contains personal data?
What establishes that retained `uri`, `payload_ref` and digest values contain no personal or re-identifying information before anonymisation succeeds?
How can anonymisation guarantee that no personal value or re-identifying link remains while preserving readable `uri` and `payload_ref` values and their targets?

quotes: A project's technical identity, status and artifact pointers are kept only where it is shown that they no longer allow re-identification and a justified purpose for keeping them is recorded; `validate` then answers `archived`. Otherwise the record is deleted whole, and `validate` answers `not_found`.
Narrowed by R0-60: the owner chooses between the two when erasing; the showing and the purpose are recorded in the governance.
judgement.why: Retention is permitted only after a governance-recorded showing that the retained identity and pointers no longer allow re-identification; otherwise the project is deleted whole.

topics.topic: Scope, increments, and concurrency use of the session access version
questions: Which changes increment the session access version, and what observable use does a caller make of it?
Which events increment the access version, and must grant, revoke, active-project change, request replacement and request answer supply the version they were made against?
What state does the access version cover, and exactly which accepted actions increment it?

quotes: the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version — no `personal_data` value (R0-32, R0-46, R0-64)
A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an older revision is refused and nothing changes. Every change is atomic.
judgement.why: This is the same question about access-version scope, mutation preconditions and stale-version behavior already assigned to State 2.

topics.topic: Unauthenticated owner sign-in actions, responses, and refusals
questions: What Registry action lets a browser without an existing session sign in, what observable result does it return, and how are missing or wrong credentials refused without contradicting the rule that no unauthenticated request answers?
Which unauthenticated owner-interface requests, at minimum the sign-in form and credential submission, are allowed to receive an answer?
Which unauthenticated action presents and processes owner sign-in, and what observable result or refusal does it produce?

quotes: No operation of Registry answers an unauthenticated caller. The owner signs in to the owner interface (R0-30); each service — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel — holds its own service token, which names it and the operations and highest disclosure class it may use.
The owner signs in to the owner interface with the owner credential and gets a protected session; the session and its expiry belong to State 2.
judgement.why: This is the same question about the unauthenticated sign-in request and its successful or refused result already answered in P14.

precedent.topic: Unauthenticated owner sign-in request and its results
quotes:
No operation of Registry answers an unauthenticated caller. The owner signs in
to the owner interface (R0-30);

The owner signs in to the owner
interface with the owner credential and gets a protected session; the session
and its expiry belong to State 2.

Anything a token does not
allow is refused.
precedent.why: The sign-in request presents the owner credential for authentication, successful authentication produces a protected session, and an unauthenticated caller receives no operation answer.

topics.topic: Validation or trust needed to exclude personal data from agent projections
questions: How can Registry guarantee that no personal value reaches an agent when agent-visible room names and pointer fields are unrestricted and uninspected, and what failure occurs when a value violates that rule?

How can Registry guarantee that no personal value reaches an agent when uninspected room names, `uri`, `payload_ref` and digest values are returned to agents and may be written by owners, services or other agent sessions?
What observable validation or trust precondition makes the no-`personal_data` guarantee true when uninspected free-text and references are returned to the agent?

quotes: It holds no owner credential and no Registry service token, never receives a `personal_data` value (R0-26), and has no administrative access to the production host, its store, configuration, secrets or deployment (R0-25).
the minimal projection of that project: its id, status, rooms and artifact pointers — no display name (R0-68), address, customer or other personal value

Room names and artifact pointers stay in it; the owner names rooms without names or addresses of people, and a producer publishes `uri`, `payload_ref` and digest without them. Registry does not inspect these values.
judgement.divergence: One implementation validates agent-visible room and pointer values and refuses values that may contain personal data, while another trusts writers and returns every uninspected value; the agent, owner and AI provider notice whether such values are refused or disclosed.
judgement.why: The unconditional no-personal-data promise has neither an enforceable trust precondition nor a failure for values that violate the stated writer convention.

topics.topic: Actions and successful or refused outcomes covered by the audit log
questions: Exactly which primary actions create audit entries: do room and artifact changes, session registration, active-project changes, access requests and answers, relationship end/resume, imports, refused changes and audit erasure count?
Does the audit log record refused attempts at significant changes, or does `outcome` describe only successful state changes?

Does the audit log include room creation, artifact publication or withdrawal, session registration, active-project changes, access requests and answers, relationship end or resume, imports, and failed changes, or is the stated list exhaustive?

quotes: Registry records only significant changes of state: changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects, restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations. Ordinary reads, agent calls and the inner steps of flows are not recorded in Registry; security events of the infrastructure are handled by the infrastructure, outside Registry.

- **Audit.** A minimal log of significant changes of state (R0-58): time, the acting principal (owner, which service, agent through Kernel), the change, the project or customer, the outcome, the contract and release version, and a confirmation id where the owner confirmed.
judgement.why: This repeats the previously judged question about the exact action and outcome coverage of the audit log.

topics.topic: Actor, action, contents, output, and failures for migration export
questions: What named actor or system produces the VPS or test-rig export, with what observable output and failures?
What product action produces the export from the VPS or test-rig Registry, who may invoke it, what does it contain, and how does failure appear?

quotes: The owner exports the chosen source and uploads the export through the owner interface; production Registry never calls the source instance and holds no credential for it (R0-18; round 6 T7).

import projects with their identity | owner, confirming, from the source the owner picks — the VPS or the test rig (R0-50, R0-54) | the projects of that source under the identities they carry, with their customers (`customer_ref` kept), objects, rooms and pointers (ids kept), links intact (R0-34, R0-44, R0-50) | any conflict with an id production holds refuses the whole import, nothing applied, and the owner may retry after correcting it; after a source's first successful import into production, importing from that source is closed and refused; the other source stays open until its own (R0-54, R0-59)

topics.topic: Cabinet Web mirror location and permitted Registry network path
questions: Where does the Cabinet Web mirror run, and through which permitted network path can it use its optional token to read Registry?
Where does the Cabinet Web mirror run, and through which permitted network boundary can it call Registry if it is given a token?

quotes: Consumer services — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, the Cabinet Web mirror. Each authenticates with its own service token (R0-27), validates a project id and reads its context in the disclosure class its token allows; the full context only with a token that allows `personal_data` (R0-43).
The Cabinet Web mirror, off active development, keeps its read only if it receives a token of its own.

Network surface — two surfaces of one process: the service API for services, reachable only inside VM Platform and over the WireGuard channel from the VPS, never from VM Agent (R0-28, R0-48); and the owner interface, reachable from outside only through the owner's VPN, over HTTPS (R0-29, R0-48).
judgement.divergence: One implementation places the mirror inside VM Platform and calls Registry locally, while another places it on the VPS and calls through WireGuard; the mirror operator and network administrator notice the deployment and permitted path.
judgement.why: The mirror is named as a possible caller but its location and corresponding trust-boundary path are not named.

topics.topic: Owner action for observing periodic retention-review inputs
questions: Through which concrete action and output can the owner obtain archived dates, relationship-ended dates and current restriction or erasure states for the periodic review?
Through which declared action can the owner observe archive dates, relationship-ended dates, restriction state and the records to consider during the periodic retention review?

quotes: Registry gives that review what it needs and nothing more:
- the date a project was archived, and the owner's mark that a customer relationship has ended (R0-49), which the owner may clear (R0-57);
read a customer | owner | name, kind, phone, e-mail, language | unknown customer refused; an erased customer answers that it was erased, with no contact data

read a project | owner; a trusted service whose token allows `personal_data` (R0-43) | the project card (any status, V1-7) with its object and rooms, its revision; the project's id stands at the top of the answer (R0-13) | unknown id refused as not found; an anonymised project answers that it was erased (R0-62); any other caller refused — Kernel for the agent reads the agent projection (R0-43)
judgement.divergence: One implementation adds the archive date, relationship-end mark and restriction or erasure state to owner reads or a retention-review view, while another exposes none of them and expects external inspection; the owner notices whether the promised periodic review can be performed through Registry.
judgement.why: Registry promises to give the review its inputs, but no declared owner action promises an output containing those inputs.

topics.topic: Project-scoped versus session-scoped agent operations
questions: Which Kernel operations are session-scoped exceptions that may run without a project in the granted set or an active project?
Which agent-authority operations are project-scoped and therefore require a granted `project_id`, and which session-level operations are allowed without one?

quotes: On every agent-authority call Registry checks three things: the calling service authenticates with its own token — being inside VM Platform authenticates nothing (R0-27); the session it names is registered; and the `project_id` is in that session's set.

read the session's access | Cabinet Kernel for one agent session; owner | the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version — no `personal_data` value (R0-32, R0-46, R0-64) | for Kernel, a session that is not registered refused like a call outside the set (R0-53); for the owner, an unknown session refused

request access to a project | Cabinet Kernel for one agent session | a pending request of that session, in free text, the owner sees in the owner interface, replacing the session's earlier pending one; the session's access does not change, and the answer says nothing about which projects exist (R0-46, R0-47) | a session that is not registered refused like a call outside the set (R0-53)
register an agent session | Cabinet Kernel | the session Registry knows, with no granted project; the owner sees it in the owner interface (R0-47) | —
judgement.why: The universal project-membership check conflicts with declared Kernel session operations that must work when the session has no granted project and that name no granted project.

topics.topic: Results, revisions, audits, and dates for repeated customer-state transitions
questions: What happens when the owner restricts an already restricted customer, lifts an unrestricted one, ends an already ended relationship, or resumes one that is not ended; in particular, may a repeated end replace the recorded date?
What are the observable result, revision effect and audit effect of repeated restriction or lift requests?
Where does the relationship-end date come from, and what are the result, revision and audit effects of repeated end or resume requests?

quotes: the Customer marked restricted, or no longer restricted where a lawful ground allows it; while restricted, its contact data stays stored and reaches no one but the owner, no project may newly name it, and every other use of its contact data is refused — Registry admits no exception; where a lawful ground allows processing, the owner lifts the restriction (R0-65); corrections of its existing projects that do not use that data go on, and `context` keeps its `customer_ref` (R0-37, R0-51, R0-55)
the Customer marked as ended on that date, or the mark cleared; archiving its projects does not end it (R0-49, R0-57, R0-60)

A project, a customer and an object carry a revision that every accepted change moves. A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an older revision is refused and nothing changes. Every change is atomic.

Registry records only significant changes of state: changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects, restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations.
judgement.why: Repeated-transition results, date replacement, revision effects and audit-event tests are operational rules owned by State 2.
